newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumer confidence rise said insignificant.
newsitem.headline: French consumer confidence rise said insignificant.

text.p: France's consumer confidence indicator, issued by statistics institute INSEE, showed a slight rise in December from November but the improvement was insignificant, economists said on Thursday.
They said the index had been of little use lately in predicting consumer behavior.
Economists said the seasonally-adjusted index appeared to have become more a reflection of consumer unhappiness than an indicator of spending plans.
The global consumer confidence index edged higher to minus 33 from minus 34 in November. "Households still appear to be pretty pessimistic," said BIP economist Nordine Naam.
Philippe Brossard of ABN-Amro Finance said the index was not much help as a forecasting tool. "It's a very puzzling index," he said.
Naam noted BIP expected household spending to show robust growth of 2.4 percent for 1996 while the consumer confidence index had suggested consumers were deeply pessimistic.
"It shows the index has not been very useful for the last year," he said.

Naam said the decoupling of the index and household consumption appeared to coincide with the introduction of the centre-right government's 1996 austerity budget aimed at preparing France to qualify for European monetary union.

The biggest improvement in the December index, which sampled the views of 2,000 households, was in people's expectations about the outlook for unemployment. The index figure for unemployment improved to 54 from 66.
INSEE forecast last month unemployment would continue to rise from its record level of 12.7 percent, peaking at 13 percent in the first half of the year, before starting to decline gradually.

While personal standard of living expectations and financial outlooks remained unchanged, the survey suggested people believed it was a better time to buy than the previous month, that index figure improving to minus 25 from minus 29.
